title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Code cut its own built-in skill from ~200k tokens to ~25k by loading reference docs ON DEMAND — the vendor's answer to context collapse is deferral, not compression
bullets.summary: The late-August Claude Code releases reduced the context cost of the built-in claude-api skill from over 200k tokens to roughly 25k, achieved not by shortening the material but by loading reference documentation only when a turn actually needs it. Shipped alongside: /permissions can now be opened while Claude is working rather than only between turns, /add-dir <path> can be used mid-turn (as can /autocompact, /theme, /help and /config), auto-generated session titles are now short and specific ("Login button bug") instead of restating the request, expired Anthropic profile credentials redirect to login instead of failing opaquely, and Bedrock plus Alpine support was added.
bullets.how: YES — this is the direct, shipped answer to the problem bullet 10 named yesterday from arXiv 2510.04618. ACE identifies BREVITY BIAS — compression pressure drops the domain insight — and this report concluded our skill files should append with provenance rather than be rewritten. Anthropic solved the same constraint from the other end: keep the full detail, but move it out of the always-loaded context and fetch it on demand, so an 87% reduction costs nothing in fidelity. That is a better fix than ours and it applies to a real problem in our library. The heavy skills — b9-answer-page-factory, the vironbox-* render family, ans-cloudrevit-appbundle, hypercube-* — are front-loaded operational manuals carrying numeric targets, gotchas and full recipes, and every one is paid for in full whether the turn needs the recipe or not. The structural move is a thin SKILL.md carrying triggers, hard rules and the decision tree, with reference material in sibling files read only when the branch is taken. Second, smaller item with immediate value: /add-dir mid-turn means a session can widen its own filesystem scope without a restart, which is the everyday version of the scope-fencing thread this report has tracked for four days.

bullets.title: CORPUS GAP — Cloudflare shipped Kitesurf, an agent-first browser with no Chromium that runs in V8 isolates on Workers at 3–7x less CPU and memory, and this report has never once mentioned it
bullets.summary: Cloudflare launched Kitesurf on Aug 6: a Rust browser runtime built for agents rather than humans, running entirely in V8 isolates on the Workers platform with no Chromium underneath. It strips tabs, themes, extensions, device sync and pixel-perfect rendering — Cloudflare's framing is that an agent 'cares about token count, context windows, scalability, performance, and costs' — and reports 3–7x lower CPU and memory for page extraction, screenshots and agent-driven browsing. It passes over 235,000 web platform tests, speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol so existing Puppeteer and Playwright automation and MCP clients work with a parameter change, and is available now in beta through Cloudflare's Browser Run at no cost subject to per-account limits.
bullets.how: YES — logged honestly as a corpus gap, not as news: it is nineteen days old and the corpus contains zero occurrences of the word, in a month where this report covered browser-use GA, the Cowork Chrome side panel and Antigravity. The reason it matters is structural. Every browser action The Construct takes — Pulse's and Lens's scans, Mallard's visibility passes, the B9 site-health sentinel, verify-and-index — runs through one Claude-in-Chrome extension attached to one Chrome on one Mac, which is the identical single-resource contention that produced the Hermes worker queue, plus a hard rule never to open a new window. A CDP-compatible runtime that executes server-side and scales horizontally is the first credible path to running those scans in parallel and OFF the Mac entirely. One caveat has to travel with the recommendation: brand9signs.com sits behind the sgcaptcha bot shield that already makes cloud curl lie about live pages, and a datacenter-resident browser will very likely be blocked the same way — so Kitesurf is a candidate for the OPEN-web half of the work (source scanning, competitor checks, engine visibility probes), while authenticated B9 verification stays in Bobby's real logged-in Chrome. Test the split before assuming either half.

bullets.title: CORPUS GAP — a multi-agent paper reports >90% internal error interception by giving agents OPPOSING incentives, which is the control this report demonstrably lacks
bullets.summary: arXiv 2601.14351 (Vijayaraghavan, Jayachandran, Murthy, Govindan, Subramanian) proposes an 'AI Office' architecture for making unreliable LLMs usable in production: teams of independent agents with strict role boundaries — planners, executors, critics, experts — sharing a common goal but holding deliberately OPPOSING incentives, coordinated through a remote code executor that keeps data transformation and tool invocation separate from the reasoning models. The reported result is over 90% of internal errors intercepted before user exposure, bought at a modest cost in action velocity.
bullets.how: YES — and the applicability is uncomfortable rather than aspirational. The Construct's roster is planners and executors: Keystone plans, Ledger models, Pulse and Lens and Mallard scan, Hermes executes. Nothing in the daily loop is incentivized to be wrong-footed by the others. The consequence is on the record in this very corpus — a false 'no signage MCP server' negative survived weeks of restatement, and seven Claude outages in twenty-four days went unlogged, and neither was caught by the agent producing the report, because the agent producing the report has no adversary. swarm-strategy-review is the nearest thing we own, but it is invoked by hand for strategy calls, not wired into a scheduled job that ships to a dashboard daily. The cheap adoption is one role, not an org chart: a critic step inside Pulse whose only job is to attempt to FALSIFY each bullet's central claim before it ships — search for the thing itself, check the date, check whether the corpus already carries it — with a bullet that survives shipping and one that does not being dropped rather than softened. That is the same four-move discipline as yesterday's bullet 9, given teeth by an incentive instead of an intention. Note also the paper's second structural point, which lands on the Hermes design: keeping tool invocation and data transformation in a separate executor from the reasoning model is what makes role boundaries enforceable rather than merely stated.

bullets.title: Both standing negatives held, and Claude posted its first clean 24 hours after a month of incidents
bullets.summary: No frontier lab — OpenAI, Google, Meta, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek or Cohere — shipped a model or material availability change in this window, now the EIGHTH consecutive scan; August's releases are all already in this corpus (Grok 4.6 on the 6th, Grok Imagine Image 2.0 and Seedance 2.5 on the 8th, Seed 2.1 Turbo on the 10th, Gemini 3.7 Flash on the 13th, GLM-5.3 on the 14th). No MCP server exposes architectural sign fabrication, wayfinding program data, sign permitting or code compliance — stated in the corrected narrow form from yesterday's bullet 7, and checked this morning by searching the directories themselves (PulseMCP, Glama, MCP.directory) rather than for news of them, with the caveat that PulseMCP paused new submissions and listing changes into mid-August, so directory lag is real and the negative is weaker than a fresh index would make it. On availability: after the Aug 24 partial outage across claude.ai, the API, Claude Code and Cowork — the seventh incident in twenty-four days, and ten logged between the 12th and the 19th alone — the trailing 24 hours to 06:10 UTC today show 100% uptime and two user-reported issues.
bullets.how: MAYBE — one clean day is not a trend and should not be reported as one, which is precisely why it belongs in the same bullet as the incident count rather than in a headline of its own. What it does is make yesterday's prescription cheap to test: a heartbeat written by every scheduled Construct job, with the dashboard rendering staleness, is only useful if we can tell a quiet day from a dead one, and today is the first day in a while where those two states were distinguishable by anything other than luck. The eighth flat scan on model capability is the more consequential half. Two months of this report's substance has been governance, packaging, scope and cost — allowlists, roles, permission intersections, context-cost reductions — not capability. For PRAGMA that is straightforwardly good news: a durable moat cannot be built on a capability gap that closes every six weeks, and a market whose frontier is flat rewards proprietary data and delivery discipline, which is exactly what the AAIR history, the answer-page corpus and the attribution chain are.

bullets.title: X shipped an Ads MCP server — the last major social ad platform to become agent-callable, and this corpus stopped tracking the thread on July 1
bullets.summary: X launched its X Ads Model Context Protocol server, announced by @XBusiness and reported Aug 23, with documentation at docs.x.com/x-ads-api/mcp. It feeds live X campaign data, analytics and creative controls into any MCP-capable client — X names Grok, Claude Code and custom agents built on the MCP SDKs — so an advertiser can launch campaigns, track performance, pause underperformers, scale winners and adjust creative or budget through natural-language prompts against real account data, without touching X's own ad-server models. The article's own dateline is internally inconsistent (published Sunday Aug 23, describing the launch as happening 'on Friday'), so treat the launch as the Aug 21-23 window rather than a single confirmed day. X is the last of the majors: Meta shipped its connector in April, TikTok at TikTok World in May, and Pinterest and Snapchat have both since announced MCP integrations.
bullets.how: For Brand 9 Signs, and it is logged as a corpus-hygiene finding as much as news. This report opened the thread on 2026-06-29 with TikTok's Ads MCP and the claim that 'the big four ad platforms are now all agent-callable,' prescribed wrapping them behind one Construct campaign-ops agent, touched it once more on 07-01, and then dropped it for eight weeks — during which Pinterest and Snapchat shipped and neither appears anywhere in the corpus, the strings 'Pinterest', 'Snapchat' and 'X Ads' returning zero matches across every file. That is the third consecutive scan to surface a gap created by stopping rather than by missing, which is now a pattern worth naming rather than a coincidence. On the substance: the June prescription is now actually buildable, because the surface is complete rather than partial, and the moat argument from bullet 4 applies directly — if every platform exposes the same MCP layer to every competitor, the advantage is not access, it is the operating model on top. For B9 specifically the honest read is narrower than the June bullet implied: B9 is a local signage business whose demand comes through the local pack, GBP and the answer-page corpus, not through paid social at a spend where campaign-ops automation pays for itself. The near-term value is the READ side — pulling campaign and audience analytics into the flywheel's attribution chain alongside GSC and GA4 — not autonomous bid management. For PRAGMA the read is the reverse and larger: a client with real paid spend can now be operated across all five platforms by one agent with one credential model, which is a concrete service line rather than a thesis.

bullets.title: CORPUS GAP — Anthropic shipped scheduled memory consolidation for agents in MAY, calls it Dreams, and this corpus has never once mentioned it across 57 files
bullets.summary: Anthropic introduced "dreaming" for Claude Managed Agents at Code with Claude on May 6: a scheduled offline process that runs BETWEEN agent sessions, reads the agent's existing memory store together with the transcripts of past sessions, and writes back a reorganised version — merging duplicates, deleting what it judges outdated, and surfacing patterns ("this user keeps making the same mistake," "this workflow always loops on step 3"). Anthropic's own analogy is hippocampal memory consolidation, the brain replaying the day and deciding what to keep, and it can be configured for automatic update or manual review. Harvey, the legal-AI startup and an early tester, reported task-completion rates rising roughly 6x once dreaming was on. It shipped alongside two siblings: `outcomes`, a self-grading loop where a separate evaluator scores the agent's output against a written rubric, and multiagent orchestration, where a lead agent fans work out to specialist subagents. Outcomes and orchestration went to public beta; Dreams stayed in research preview behind an access request, and has been quietly widened since — the platform release notes add Fable 5 and Sonnet 5 support on Jul 10 and Opus 5 on Aug 1.
bullets.how: and this is the largest corpus gap this report has found, not because the feature is obscure but because it is the vendor-native form of something Bobby already built by hand and runs every day. `praxis-inbox.md` is a memory store. The `self-improving-loop` skill is a consolidation process. This very file is a transcript of past sessions. The whole architecture — capture the correction, write the lesson, feed it back so the mistake does not repeat — is dreaming, implemented manually, with a human scheduler and no evaluator. Three specific reads follow. First, `outcomes` is the falsification step from bullet 3 already built and in public beta: a separate evaluator scoring output against a written rubric is exactly the adversary this report concluded it lacks, and it does not need to be invented. Second, Dreams addresses a real decay in our own loop — the PRAXIS inbox only ever appends, so it grows monotonically and nothing merges duplicates or retires stale lessons, which is the failure mode ACE calls context collapse arriving from the opposite direction to brevity bias. Third, the honest caveat: Dreams is research-preview, access-gated, and scoped to Managed Agents rather than to Cowork or Claude Code sessions, so the near-term move is to steal the DESIGN — a scheduled consolidation pass over the inbox that merges and retires rather than only appends — not to wait on the feature. Note also the security literature that grew up around this feature: a memory store that rewrites itself between sessions is a persistence surface, and anything that reaches the transcript reaches the next session's premises.

bullets.title: RE-CHECK PAID OFF — Xnurta's MCP Phase 2 went GA today with "action spaces": permissions as persistent policy instead of per-action approval
bullets.summary: Xnurta, whose retail-media MCP server this report logged on 08-19 and 08-20 as evidence of vertical data vendors publishing an MCP layer instead of an API portal, reached general availability on Phase 2 of that roadmap TODAY, Aug 25, after a closed beta that opened Aug 11. Phase 2 is "Managed Group Management" — creating, updating and deleting managed groups, scheduling bulk operations, and configuring ACTION SPACES: configurable boundaries that determine what an AI assistant is permitted to change. Xnurta's framing is the load-bearing part: action spaces establish permissions as persistent POLICY rather than requiring a human to approve every AI-generated action, which is how the company describes moving MCP "from analysis to execution."
bullets.how: and it is worth being explicit that this bullet exists because of the discipline prescribed four hours ago. The 10:00 lesson was that a bullet shipping a YES should go onto a DATED RE-CHECK LIST rather than be trusted to recur; Xnurta was re-checked on that basis and had shipped its next phase the same morning. The list works, and one afternoon is enough evidence to keep it. On the substance, this is the same thread as the allowlists and permission intersections tracked on 08-24, arriving from the commercial side rather than the vendor side, and the pattern is now visible in three places at once: Anthropic's `allowed_domains`/`blocked_domains` on managed-agent tools, Zenity's $125M for agent identity and permissions, and now a mid-market martech vendor treating scoped authority as a shippable product feature. The reason it matters to The Construct specifically is that our own governance is per-action and human-in-the-loop — Mallard drafts and every live-site write is approval-gated, Hermes holds the credentials and executes what it is handed. That is correct while trust is being established and it is the reason nothing has gone badly wrong, but it does not scale to many concurrent client pods, and the industry is converging on the alternative: declare the boundary once as policy, let the agent move freely inside it, audit afterwards. For PRAGMA this is the more useful half — an operator service whose value is that a client's agent is SAFELY autonomous needs a stated action space per client, and that artifact does not exist for any client today. The negative worth carrying: no one, including Xnurta, has published evidence that policy-scoped autonomy holds up under adversarial input, so treat the model as the direction of travel rather than as proven.

praxis_lesson: Third fire of the day; the 06:00 report and the 10:00 addendum were both verified and appended to, not rewritten. The dated re-check list prescribed at 10:00 was used for the first time and immediately produced bullet 7 — Xnurta, logged on 08-19 as a pattern example, shipped MCP Phase 2 to GA this morning with 'action spaces': permissions declared once as persistent policy rather than approved action by action, which is the same scoped-authority thread as Anthropic's allowed_domains and Zenity's $125M arriving from the commercial side. A thread that gets a YES is worth revisiting on a date; that is now demonstrated rather than argued. The larger finding should sting: Anthropic shipped scheduled memory consolidation for agents in MAY — Dreams, which reads an agent's memory store plus its past transcripts and writes back a merged, pruned version, with Harvey reporting roughly 6x task completion — and across 57 files this corpus has never contained the word, though it appears twice in Anthropic's own release notes (Jul 10, Aug 1). Dreams is the vendor-native form of machinery Bobby already runs by hand: praxis-inbox.md is the memory store, self-improving-loop is the consolidation pass, this report is the transcript. Two things follow and neither needs research-preview access — our inbox only ever APPENDS, so it grows monotonically while nothing merges duplicates or retires stale lessons, and it needs a scheduled consolidating pass; and the sibling feature 'outcomes' is already in public beta, a separate evaluator scoring output against a written rubric, which is precisely the adversary bullet 3 said we lack, shipped rather than hypothetical. Three scans in a row found their best item in something we stopped tracking; this one found it in something we never started. Frontier negative held for the NINTH consecutive scan (GLM-5.2 Turbo, Aug 17, still the most recent).
